name: BitNet
one_liner: Microsoft's toolkit for running a special kind of ultra-compressed AI model that uses far less memory and battery than normal, so it can run fast on ordinary laptops and phones instead of needing a powerful server.
buyer: A device manufacturer or app developer who wants to put AI features directly on a phone, laptop, or embedded device without draining the battery or needing an internet connection.
business_use_cases: An app developer builds an offline, battery-friendly AI assistant feature into a mobile app using these ultra-efficient models, avoiding ongoing cloud inference costs.
A device maker (smart speaker, in-car assistant, industrial sensor) embeds a lightweight on-device model for voice or text features without needing a powerful chip.
A company building AI tools for field workers with unreliable internet (construction, utilities, logistics) ships an offline AI assistant that runs entirely on a laptop.

money_ideas.idea: License a packaged, optimized on-device AI assistant built on this to hardware makers for a per-unit fee.
Consulting service helping companies port an existing cloud AI feature to run offline on-device using this framework.

steal_this: This is deep infrastructure for engineers, not something a non-technical buyer would ever touch directly — value only shows up once someone builds a finished product on top of it.
